subject: Post-call: TrustMed eval orchestration & scoring plan
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@trustedclinic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 18:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: TrustMed eval orchestration & scoring plan

Hi Emily / Amit — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before engineering kicks off the eval run: 

Summary of ask
- You want a focused, customer-specific benchmark to validate triage & discharge-summary suggestions across a sample of 10k anonymized notes. Primary concerns: PHI handling, entity extraction accuracy, and overall actionability.

Redwood proposal (high level)
- Recommended model shortlist for the pilot: Redwood-curated Llama-2-instruct (70B, 4-bit), Mistral-Instruct-32B, and Redwood-Opt-13B (int8). We’ll run each under the same prompt bank and scoring functions.
- Two evaluation tracks: (A) short-context triage (single-encounter notes, <=1024 tokens), (B) long-context summarization & action extraction (multi-encounter, up to 8k tokens).
- Expected timeline: dataset upload + schema confirmation (3 business days), initial run (48–72h), scoring & calibrations (3–5 days).

What we need from TrustMed to proceed
1) Confirm you can produce a 10k note sample in the attached NDJSON schema (trustmed_eval_schema.ndjson). We included example rows in the file.
2) Decide whether you require Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for PHI — this affects onboarding time.
3) Share a short prompt set (5–10 seed prompts) you use in production for triage/summarization, so we can mirror them exactly.

Attachments & links
- Attached: trustmed_eval_schema.ndjson (schema + mini-sample)
- Drive: shared benchmarking doc & scoring rubric (link below).

Next steps
- If you confirm dataset readiness and deployment preference, we’ll schedule a 30m ops call (Mar 10–11) to walk through upload and provide a presigned S3 endpoint.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Marissa to lead the upload and scoring setup.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior SDR, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Hart <emily.hart@trustedclinic.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@trustedclinic.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 01:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: TrustMed eval orchestration & scoring plan

Thanks Grace — this is very clear and helpful. Quick answers: 
- We can produce the 10k sample but we need to confirm PHI redaction steps. Our security/compliance team requires either (1) on-prem/private deployment or (2) redaction + hashing of identifiers before upload. Which is faster for an initial pilot?
- We will attach an example export (truncated) later today for schema confirmation — it contains patient_id (hashed), encounter_text, encounter_type, and clinical_tags.
- We can share a small prompt bank (5 prompts) by EOD.

One additional ask: procurement prefers a short, non-binding MOU describing data handling for the pilot. Can Redwood share a templated data processing addendum?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — happy to join the ops call on Mar 10.

— Emily
Dr. Emily Hart
Director of Clinical Innovation, TrustMed Clinical
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Hart <emily.hart@trustedclinic.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: TrustMed eval orchestration & scoring plan

Hi Emily — copying the ops playbook here and specifics for the NDJSON we expect (this will speed ingestion into our eval runner):

Required fields (NDJSON)
- note_id (string) — opaque id, can be hashed
- patient_id (string) — hashed or tokenized; if you can provide a stable pseudonym mapping that’s ideal
- encounter_text (string) — full clinical note text (utf-8)
- encounter_type (string) — triage, discharge_summary, inpatient_note, etc.
- reference_labels (object as JSON string) — ground truth for the scoring (see example row in attached schema)
- metadata (object as JSON string) — facility_id, timezone, encounter_date (ISO)

Example row (single-line NDJSON) — included in trustmed_eval_schema.ndjson for copy/paste.

Scoring rubric (proposal)
- Entity extraction: micro-F1 on concept-level labels (0–1 float)
- Actionability: human-graded 0–2 scale per note (0 = incorrect/misleading, 1 = partially useful, 2 = actionable and correct)
- Summarization ROUGE-L / BERTScore for high-level fidelity checks
- Composite score = weighted sum (entities 45%, actionability 40%, fidelity 15%) — we can tune weights if you prefer.

Upload options
- Preferred: presigned S3 (we provide endpoint) — simpler and encrypted in transit.
- Alternative: secure upload to your VPC if you require on-prem-only transfer.

I attached a short PDF with step-by-step upload instructions and the mutual action plan workbook that Grace referenced. Also flagged: if you require Private deployment, provisioning will add ~5 business days.

Let me know when you upload the sample and we will run a small smoke test (100 notes) and share preliminary metrics.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Emily Hart <emily.hart@trustedclinic.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 11:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: TrustMed eval orchestration & scoring plan

Couple technical notes from the model/eval side: 

Model suggestions & variants
- Baseline: Redwood-Opt-13B (int8) — cheap and good for entity extraction baseline.
- Candidate high-capacity: Llama-2-70B-instruct (4-bit QAT) — best chance to hit actionability target but watch for subtle hallucinations on rare conditions.
- Mistral-Instruct-32B — good tradeoff for longer-context summarization.

Quality regression checks
- We will run calibration evaluations: seed prompts + 30 synthetic perturbations per prompt to detect sensitivity.
- Run a delta-analysis vs a locked baseline (we’ll snapshot baseline model responses and compute entity-level diffs). If entity F1 drops >5 points or actionability average drops >0.15, we flag a potential regression.

Scoring details (automated)
- Entity extraction: span-normalized exact-match + fuzzy match (edit distance threshold) for clinical terms.
- Actionability: we’ll run crowd-human grading via our scorer pool — provide 200 human ratings per model per track for statistical confidence.

Prompts & prompt bank
- Please include your canonical production prompts. Also include 5–10 negative-control prompts (edge cases) you’ve seen fail in production.

Notes on quantization risk
- 4-bit quantized weights can introduce systematic tokenization shifts that affect rare-term recall. For clinical entities, we’ll prioritize running at least one full-precision pass on a 500-note subset to verify sensitive terms before accepting quantized results.

I’ll prepare the baseline snapshot and a small script to compute the composite score; will share repo link in the drive doc shortly.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: TrustMed eval orchestration & scoring plan

Great — thanks everyone. Emily, next practical steps for us: 
1) If you confirm PHI handling preference (private vs redacted upload) we’ll attach the appropriate DPA addendum template for your legal team.
2) Please upload the 10k sample (or a 1k subset to start) to the presigned S3 link we’ll send after the ops call.
3) Send the prompt bank + 5 negative-control prompts by EOD so Rishi can seed the calibration runs.
4) Ops call: proposed slots Mar 10 at 14:00 or Mar 11 at 09:00 ET — which works?

We’ll aim for a small smoke test within 48 hours of upload and share a first-pass dashboard. I’ll attach the mutual_action_plan.xlsx and loop in our legal contact after you confirm deployment preference.

If all good, I’ll schedule the ops call and send the presigned URL and the DPA template.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior SDR, Redwood Inference
